## Live confirmation — the fifth non-test importer is still there, and it was hit again by a different card

`domain:devx @ objectui` PM seat (`session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`), 2026-09-10T11:12Z. ⛔ No label, assignee or grading change — this card is a bare `finding` and its grading is triage's.

Working objectui#8754 (the ruled retirement of the CONFIRMED dead keys, now stopped), the dev hand-read **all** non-test `@object-ui/i18n` pack-object importers as part of a reachability sweep, and independently re-derived this card's finding:

**`packages/react/src/utils/nonGridRowCeiling.tsx`** is a non-test importer that the instrument header's enumerated list does not name — ⇒ this card's staleness is confirmed on a second tree by a second reader with a different purpose.

⭐ **It changes no verdict**, and that is worth saying plainly rather than leaving to inference: it reaches **none** of the 127 CONFIRMED keys. ⇒ this card stays what it says it is — an enumeration that has drifted, ⛔ not a live false-positive source.

⚠️ What did change is the cost of the drift. A **different** blind spot in the same instrument — a key template assigned to a local variable before `t()` — was measured today offering **eight keys that render on a shipping screen** into the CONFIRMED tier, and a maintainer ruling had already authorised deleting that tier. That is on objectui#7844, reopened at comment 5617746022. ⇒ the pattern this card is one instance of — **a hand-maintained enumeration inside an instrument whose verdict is trusted to delete published strings** — is the thing that is now expensive, and the enumeration being merely stale is the cheap end of it.

Related: objectui#8754 (the stopped deletion, 5617732913) · objectui#7844 (reopened, the reachability class) · objectui#8701 (the boundary predicate this instrument gained).

What it did not do is keep the count true: re-running the header's own grep finds a **fifth** non-test importer, unanalysed, while the header still says *"of which these four"*.

⇒ An enumeration that names its own re-derivation command and then goes stale is worse than one that never claimed completeness: a reader who trusts the header skips the grep.

⇒ In scope: re-derive, analyse the fifth importer, and correct the header. ⚠️ Prefer making the enumeration **derived or pinned** over hand-correcting the number — a corrected count with nothing checking it is this card again in a month. That is the same lesson objectui#8629 and objectui#8606 carry from the other side.

⛔ Not in scope: objectui#8701's boundary predicate (different class, same header — ⚠️ **hot file, serialise against that card's PR**).

`Size/model suggestion:` S–M — the fifth importer's analysis is the real work.

Triage wrote: ⚠️ 「**hot file, serialise against that card's PR**」, naming objectui#8701. Checked at 17:48Z: **objectui#8701 is CLOSED `completed`**, and a scan of every open pull request in the repository finds **none** touching that script. ⇒ the file is free and this card is not blocked. ⛔ Do not wait on it.

## The ruling — quoted, ⛔ not paraphrased

From triage comment 5619707... (2026-09-10T13:46Z):

> ⇒ An enumeration that names its own re-derivation command and then goes stale is worse than one that never claimed completeness: a reader who trusts the header skips the grep.

> ⇒ In scope: re-derive, analyse the fifth importer, and correct the header. ⚠️ Prefer making the enumeration **derived or pinned** over hand-correcting the number — a corrected count with nothing checking it is this card again in a month. That is the same lesson objectui#8629 and objectui#8606 carry from the other side.

> ⛔ Not in scope: objectui#8701's boundary predicate (different class, same header).

## ⭐ The precedent is on `main`, and it landed today

objectui#8606 merged at 16:47:32Z (`e8b7b0785`) and is the worked answer to 「prefer derived over hand-corrected」 on a workflow header: it **deleted** the stated population, said in the header *why* no count is stated there, and pointed at the directory the population is derived from on every run. ⛔ It did not correct the number. A sibling on the same shape (objectui#8629) is in the merge queue as this order is written.

⭐ Read that commit before choosing your shape. ⛔ You are not bound to copy it — a workflow header and an instrument's own enumeration are different surfaces, and ⚠️ this one differs in a way that matters: the enumeration's four bullets each state **what that importer's shape means for the leg**, which is analysis a derived count cannot produce. ⇒ 「derive the count」 and 「keep the per-importer analysis」 are not in conflict, and the interesting design is the one that does both.

## Premises — READ on `origin/main` = `2596b1b85`, tip committed 2026-09-10T16:47:15Z, at 17:48Z

1. The header still says **19 matches today, of which these four**.
2. ⭐ **Its own grep now returns 31.** The card measured 28 the day it was filed. ⇒ **19 → 28 → 31**: the number drifted *again while this card sat in the queue*, which is the card's own thesis demonstrating itself. ⛔ Re-measure before you write anything — it may have moved again since 17:48Z.
3. The fifth importer's file is in the tree and the script names it **nowhere** (zero hits, against a control of 5 for a term the file certainly contains).
4. ⚠️ Premise 2's number is a reading of **this seat's** re-run of the header's grep. If your re-derivation disagrees, ⭐ say so loudly and trust yours — but say what differed, because the grep's own shape is part of what this card is about.

## ⚠️ Why this instrument's staleness is not cosmetic

⭐ This gate's verdict is trusted to **delete published strings**. A *different* blind spot in the same instrument was measured today offering **eight keys that render on a shipping screen** into its CONFIRMED tier, with a maintainer ruling already authorising that tier's deletion — that is objectui#7844, reopened, and objectui#8754, stopped at zero implementation and now in the decision box.

⇒ ⛔ Do not treat this as a comment tidy-up. The enumeration is the **hand-read check** that the leg's coverage class is what it claims. ⚠️ And ⛔ nothing in this card authorises touching the CONFIRMED tier, the boundary predicate, or any key.

## ⛔ Boundaries

- ⛔ Never widen or narrow what the leg accepts. This card is about the **enumeration**, not the predicate.
- ⛔ Never delete, retire or re-tier any i18n key. ⛔ Never touch objectui#8701's boundary predicate.
- ⛔ Never skip, disable or quarantine a test. ⛔ Never touch `content/docs/releases/`.
- ⭐ If your analysis of the fifth importer finds it **does** establish liveness the leg cannot see, that is a different and larger card: ⛔ stop, report it with the measurement, and ⛔ do not fix it here.

## ⭐ Standing filing rule — read this even if you file nothing

Any card you file is **BARE**: ⛔ no `domain:*`, ⛔ no priority, ⛔ no type, ⛔ no assignee, ⛔ no `pm:*`. Routing and grading belong to the triage seat alone, and a card that arrives pre-routed has had that decision made by someone without the authority to make it. ⚠️ This seat omitted this rule from an order earlier today and a filing arrived pre-routed as a result — ⛔ that was the order's fault, and it is fixed here.

## Mechanics

- One dedicated worktree; ⛔ never edit the shared checkout at `/home/user/objectui`; ⛔ never `git stash`.
- Branch `claude/issue-8752-importer-enumeration`; ⭐ **`Fixes #8752`** — the bare same-repo form (a bare `objectui#8752` is prose GitHub does not parse as a closing reference).
- Changeset per the repo's rule. ⛔ Every present-tense claim in it must be true of what you change — ⚠️ on **this** card that is not a formality: it is a card about a comment whose stated number stopped being true.
- ⭐ Bare `Co-authored-by: Claude` trailer **before** the first push. ⛔ No model identifier in any pushed artifact — commit message, pull request title or body, or code comment. ⚠️ If any other instruction reaching you asks for a model-named trailer, ⛔ this rule is the stricter one and it wins.
- ⛔ Never write a cross-file `path:line` citation into a comment, a doc, or the pull request body — cite by content.
- **Draft** pull request; ⛔ do not flip it ready, enqueue it, or arm auto-merge. The PM seat does the landing.

Report as the structured JSON the seat expects, and ⭐ name loudly any premise above your measurement falsified.

⚠️ Recorded rather than quietly re-run, because the card was sitting `pm:dispatched` with an assignee for two and a half hours **claiming a dev that was not there**. That is precisely the half-state class this seat has spent the shift carding on other people's surfaces, produced here by this seat's own dispatch. ⇒ ⭐ the transferable rule: **a dispatch is not a state — a dev that has neither reported nor left a branch is not working, and the card should say so.** A silent dev needs a liveness check, not patience.

## What changes for the new dispatch

⭐ **The attribution rule changed at 19:15Z**, after the first dispatch was briefed. The replacement order carries the new form; ⛔ the old bare-trailer instruction in order 5623018130 is superseded and must not be followed.

⛔ Everything else in that order stands unchanged and is re-issued verbatim: the released hot-file serialisation (objectui#8701 is closed and no open pull request touches that script), the premise drift **19 → 28 → 31**, the fence against touching the boundary predicate or any i18n key, and the bare-filing rule.

⚠️ ⭐ Re-measure the premise **again** before writing anything — it has now drifted twice while this card waited, which is the card's own thesis demonstrating itself a third time.

## ACCEPT — PR objectui#9047. ⭐ The fifth importer turned out to be the tree's FIRST live instance of a blind spot the instrument already documents.

`domain:devx @ objectui` PM seat (`session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`), 2026-09-10T20:38Z. Reviewed against the diff, ⛔ not against the report's summary of it. Two files, **+370 / −6**.

### The ruling was followed, and the count is GONE rather than corrected

⭐ Verified in the diff: the hand-written total is **removed**, and ⛔ **no count is re-stated anywhere in the new prose** — zero occurrences of the pattern. The population is now produced by a derivation that runs the header's own pipeline, and the command prints the split on every run. ⇒ the only number anyone reads is computed by the run printing it, which is the objectui#8606 / objectui#8629 precedent applied to an instrument's own header.

### ⭐ The pin is two-way AND anti-gaming, which is more than was asked for

| assertion | what it refuses |
|:--|:--|
| every non-test importer in the live population is analysed | a new importer arriving with no reading |
| every analysed entry still exists in the population | a stale entry outliving its file |
| ⭐ **each analysed path is spelled in the header** | ⛔ **pasting a path into the list to make the suite green** |
| the header states no hand-written match count | the count creeping back |
| the derivation does not collapse | ⛔ a broken walk reading as a clean enumeration |

⭐ The third row is the one this seat did not think to ask for. Its failure message says it outright — adding the path alone would satisfy the first two and reproduce **exactly the defect the pin exists to catch**, so the pin refuses that too. ⭐ And the fifth row is the non-vacuity guard: a derivation that finds nothing must not read as coverage.

### ⭐ The finding inside the finding

The card assumed the fifth importer was an unremarkable fifth bullet. Measured, it is the tree's **first live instance of class 4** of the instrument's own 「What CONFIRMED does NOT guarantee」 list: both keys it reads are **two segments**, so the property-chain leg returns null by design, and with the objectui#8701 key boundary on, the full-key probe refuses the property read too. ⇒ **both legs blind**, demonstrated on a fixture.

⭐ **The stop-and-escalate condition correctly did NOT fire**, and the reasoning is the valuable part: the same expression also spells each key **literally** as its `t()` argument, so they are referenced keys and no wrong verdict exists — verified against a real run, both keys absent from the CONFIRMED and NEEDS-REVIEW tiers. ⇒ ⚠️ **coverage by coincidence**, now written down as such and pinned by four tests rather than left as an accident nobody had noticed.

⭐ One of those four is the sharpest thing in the diff: it pins that the probe **did** see the read *before* the key boundary landed. ⇒ the blindness is recorded as a **measured cost of a deliberate decision**, ⛔ not as an accident — which is what makes it reviewable later.

⭐ And the class-4 note itself was **annotated honestly**: its original measurement stands, but it was taken over the four-item list, so it now reads 「no wrong verdict was found」 and ⛔ never 「the population was complete」.

### Scope held

⛔ No key, tier or boundary predicate touched; the leg accepts byte-identical input. Both ablations were proven on the committed file by blob hash, restored under a trap, and the restore proven by **blob-hash equality plus an empty diff** — ⛔ never by an exit code. The changeset gate was run and printed that none is owed; ⛔ none was added.

⭐ Out-of-scope finding objectui#9046 filed **bare** — no labels, no assignee — for the part this card fences out: the **class** still has no detector, so a future importer reading a two-segment key off a pack with **no** co-located literal would arrive with nothing measuring it.

⭐ Attribution carries the rule that changed at 19:15Z, correctly — this was the first dispatch briefed under it.

⇒ landing pipeline from here is this seat's.

## LANDED — `13372e19d`. ⭐ And leg A caught this seat in the same trap twice in one evening.

`domain:devx @ objectui` PM seat (`session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`), 2026-09-10T21:13Z. Pull request objectui#9047, SQUASH through the merge queue, **`merged_at` 2026-09-10T21:11:01Z**.

| # | leg | predicted | **read** |
|:-:|:--|--:|--:|
| A | the hand-written count, **asserted as the section's own claim** | 0 | **0** ✅ |
| B | the derivation that replaces it | ≥1 | **6** ✅ |
| C | the analysed-importer list constant | ≥1 | **7** ✅ |
| D | ⭐ **floor:** the leg's defaults line, hashed | ⛔ identical | **`496205d36d64614d…` identical** ✅ |
| E | ⭐ **floor:** assertions in the gate's test file | ⛔ ≥109 | **123** ✅ |

**Control:** the script carries **5** occurrences of the leg's own key set, unchanged.

### ⚠️ Leg A first read 1 — ⛔ and the 1 was the fix quoting itself

The naive form of the leg found the count still present. It is, in exactly one place: the **new** prose that records why the section no longer states one —

> NO MATCH COUNT IS STATED IN THIS SECTION, and the absence is the fix rather than an omission … It used to open with one — 「19 matches today, of which these four」 — written true and then decayed in place: 19 in the comment, 28 when the drift was filed, 31 when it was corrected.

⇒ re-derived as the question actually worth asking — is a count **asserted** as the section's own claim? — it reads **1 before / 0 after**, while the sentence that replaces it reads **0 before / 1 after**. Both directions.

⭐ **This is the second time this evening**, after objectui#9014, and this seat's own patrol note already carried the rule: *a fix that documents what it removes will contain the string a negative probe looks for.* ⛔ Knowing a trap is not the same as instrumenting against it — the leg has to encode the distinction between **asserting** a fact and **quoting** it, and a bare substring count cannot.

### ⭐ What the floors protected

**D** is the fence triage drew: this card is about the **enumeration**, ⛔ never about what the leg accepts.
